stocks.name: Micron Technology
stocks.thesis: Micron is positioned as a critical high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and DRAM supplier riding the accelerated AI training and inference capex cycle, with 196% YoY revenue growth indicating secured design wins across hyperscaler GPU clusters. At 9.2x forward PE against hypergrowth revenue, the valuation discounts execution risk and potential supply normalization post-2025 when AI infrastructure capex moderates.

stocks.name: Marvell Technology
stocks.thesis: Marvell is capturing accelerating demand for data center interconnect and custom AI processors as hyperscalers scale training clusters, with 27.6% YoY revenue growth positioning it as a core beneficiary of the multi-year GPU/accelerator proliferation cycle. However, the 33.7x forward PE reflects peak growth expectations and leaves minimal margin for execution missteps or cyclical normalization in capex spending.

stocks.name: Nvidia
stocks.thesis: NVDA's 85.2% YoY revenue growth demonstrates sustained demand dominance in GPU-accelerated AI training and inference, positioning it as the critical bottleneck supplier in the current infrastructure buildout cycle where compute capacity remains the limiting factor for LLM deployment. At 16.7x forward PE, the valuation has normalized from peak multiples, pricing in realistic growth deceleration while still capturing the structural shift toward AI capex concentration in hyperscaler hands.

stocks.name: HPE
stocks.thesis: HPE's 18.4% YoY revenue growth positions it as a direct beneficiary of enterprise AI infrastructure spending, with a forward PE of 15.8x offering reasonable valuation entry for a company riding secular GPU server and edge AI compute demand tailwinds. The subsector focus on AI Server Systems provides exposure to the capex-intensive phase of enterprise AI deployment without premium NVIDIA multiples.

stocks.name: Super Micro Computer
stocks.thesis: SMCI is capturing outsized demand from hyperscalers' GPU server buildout with 122.7% YoY revenue growth, positioning it as a critical pick-and-shovel beneficiary in the AI infrastructure capex cycle that will likely sustain through 2025. At a 14.3x forward PE, the valuation appropriately reflects hypergrowth while remaining disciplined relative to peers, offering asymmetric upside if AI capex accelerates further.

stocks.name: Dell Technologies
stocks.thesis: Dell's 87.5% YoY revenue growth positions it as a direct beneficiary of hyperscaler capex acceleration for AI inference and training infrastructure, with strong demand visibility in its PowerEdge GPU server lines. At a 21.2x forward PE, the valuation is reasonable relative to growth magnitude, though compressed relative to pure-play AI infrastructure peers, suggesting market underpricing of Dell's AI exposure within its broader portfolio.

stocks.name: Broadcom
stocks.thesis: Broadcom is capturing outsized growth in the AI infrastructure cycle through its dominant position in data center interconnect silicon and high-speed SerDes IP, with 29.5% YoY revenue growth significantly outpacing semiconductor industry averages as hyperscalers scale GPU clusters and networking fabrics. At a 24.2x forward PE, the valuation is justified by durable 25%+ growth runway as AI capex cycles remain in early innings, particularly in custom silicon and networking ASICs for major cloud providers.

stocks.name: AMD
stocks.thesis: AMD is capturing accelerating AI infrastructure demand through its EPYC data center CPUs and MI GPU portfolio, leveraging its cost-competitiveness against NVIDIA while benefiting from the 37.8% YoY revenue growth trajectory. However, the 39.7x forward PE embeds aggressive expectations for sustained market share gains in a consolidating accelerator market where NVIDIA commands ~80% mindshare.

stocks.name: Western Digital
stocks.thesis: WDC is positioned as a critical beneficiary of accelerating AI data center buildout, with 45.5% YoY revenue growth indicating strong demand for enterprise SSDs and HDD storage solutions serving model training and inference infrastructure. However, the 30.2x forward PE reflects this opportunity being substantially priced in, leaving limited margin of safety for execution risks in a cyclical storage market.

stocks.name: Cisco
stocks.thesis: Cisco is positioned as a critical chokepoint in enterprise AI infrastructure, with 12% YoY revenue growth reflecting steady demand for high-margin switching and routing hardware that underpins data center AI deployments; however, the 25.2x forward PE prices in significant AI-driven acceleration that requires sustained capex cycles from cloud hyperscalers to materialize.

stocks.name: Oracle
stocks.thesis: Oracle is capturing enterprise AI infrastructure demand through its specialized cloud offerings, with 21.7% YoY revenue growth positioning it as a consolidation play for legacy database customers migrating workloads to AI-native architectures. At 28.1x forward PE, the valuation reflects execution risk on converting its installed base into higher-margin AI services faster than hyperscalers can disintermediate the relationship.

stocks.name: Lumentum Holdings
stocks.thesis: Lumentum is positioned as a critical optical connectivity bottleneck beneficiary in the AI infrastructure buildout, with 90.1% YoY revenue growth indicating strong demand for high-speed interconnect components essential for hyperscaler data center expansion. However, the 47.2x forward PE reflects aggressive market pricing that assumes sustained hypergrowth and provides minimal margin for execution missteps or demand normalization.

stocks.name: TSMC
stocks.thesis: TSMC's 35.1% YoY revenue growth reflects sustained AI chip demand from both hyperscalers and custom silicon players, positioning it as the critical manufacturing chokepoint for the entire AI infrastructure buildout cycle. At a 21.4x forward PE, the valuation is compressed relative to both historical averages and growth rate, offering alpha exposure to AI capex cycles with limited multiple expansion risk.

stocks.name: Coherent Corp
stocks.thesis: Coherent is positioned as a critical enabler of the AI infrastructure buildout through its optical connectivity solutions, which are essential for high-bandwidth interconnects in data centers scaling large language models and GPU clusters. At 44.6x forward PE with 20.5% YoY revenue growth, the company is pricing in significant margin expansion and sustained demand, making it a leveraged play on AI capex acceleration—but valuation assumes execution flawlessness in a capacity-constrained supply environment.

stocks.name: Arista Networks
stocks.thesis: Arista is capturing disproportionate share of AI datacenter networking spend through its high-density switching platforms and software-defined networking stack, with 35% YoY revenue growth demonstrating sustained demand from hyperscaler capex cycles. At 35.8x forward PE, the valuation embeds aggressive growth expectations that leave minimal margin for deceleration in AI infrastructure investment cycles or increased competition from Broadcom/Nvidia.

stocks.name: Qualcomm
stocks.thesis: Qualcomm is strategically positioned to capture the edge AI inference wave as enterprises deploy on-device processing for latency-sensitive applications, with its Snapdragon and custom silicon addressing the $200B+ addressable market beyond data center GPUs. However, the -3.5% YoY revenue contraction suggests near-term smartphone/mobile headwinds are offsetting early AI infrastructure wins, requiring 2-3 quarters of positive acceleration to justify the 23.6x forward multiple.

stocks.name: Vertiv Holdings
stocks.thesis: Vertiv is positioned as a critical beneficiary of hyperscaler capex acceleration, with 30% YoY revenue growth reflecting robust demand for data center power distribution and thermal management—essential infrastructure that scales with AI compute buildout. However, the 35.7x forward PE prices in substantial margin expansion and sustained growth velocity, leaving limited room for execution missteps in a competitive supply environment.

stocks.name: Quanta Services
stocks.thesis: Quanta Services is positioned as a critical execution play in the AI infrastructure buildout cycle, capturing secular demand for data center power distribution, cooling infrastructure, and electrical installation as hyperscalers race to deploy GPU clusters at scale. At 43.3x forward PE with 26.3% YoY revenue growth, the company is pricing in sustained double-digit expansion, but the valuation multiple leaves minimal margin for execution missteps or competitive pressure from integrated infrastructure providers.

stocks.name: Amazon
stocks.thesis: Amazon's AWS is capturing disproportionate AI infrastructure demand through vertically integrated advantages (custom chips, networking, data center density) while 16.6% revenue growth masks accelerating cloud segment expansion driven by GenAI workload migration. At 27.4x forward PE, the valuation reflects justified re-rating for infrastructure-as-a-service oligopoly positioning, but requires sustained margin expansion to justify further multiple expansion.

stocks.name: CoreWeave
stocks.thesis: CoreWeave is capturing accelerating demand for specialized GPU cloud infrastructure as enterprises move inference and fine-tuning workloads off hyperscaler platforms, with 111.6% YoY revenue growth indicating market share gains during peak AI infrastructure deployment cycle. The negative forward PE reflects pre-profitability positioning typical of high-growth infrastructure plays, but warrants proof of path to positive unit economics as the market matures.

stocks.name: Applied Materials
stocks.thesis: AMAT is a critical choke-point supplier in the AI infrastructure buildout, with 11.4% YoY revenue growth reflecting sustained demand for semiconductor manufacturing equipment as foundries scale capacity for AI chips; however, the 27.8x forward PE prices in significant upside already, requiring flawless execution across both logic and memory node transitions.

stocks.name: KLA Corporation
stocks.thesis: KLA's 11.5% YoY revenue growth positions it as a critical enabler of AI chip manufacturing, capturing secular demand from both advanced logic (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel) and memory (HBM) capacity expansions. However, at 38.5x forward PE, the market is pricing in acceleration well beyond current growth rates, leaving minimal margin for execution misses or capex cycle softness from hyperscalers.

stocks.name: Alphabet
stocks.thesis: Alphabet's 21.8% YoY revenue growth reflects sustained demand for Google Cloud's AI infrastructure services, positioning it as a critical beneficiary of the enterprise AI buildout cycle competing directly against AWS and Azure. However, at 26.2x forward PE, the stock has priced in significant margin expansion and market share gains, leaving limited margin of safety if cloud growth deceleration emerges or competitive intensity increases.

stocks.name: Meta
stocks.thesis: Meta's 33.1% YoY revenue growth reflects aggressive monetization of its AI inference infrastructure and recommendation systems across 3B+ users, positioning it as a primary beneficiary of the shift from training-centric to inference-at-scale economics. At 17.5x forward PE, the stock prices in sustained double-digit growth without premium multiple expansion, offering asymmetric upside if AI ad targeting ROI drives advertiser spending acceleration beyond consensus models.

stocks.name: ASML
stocks.thesis: ASML is the critical chokepoint supplier of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography equipment essential for sub-3nm chip manufacturing, positioning it as a direct beneficiary of the AI chip arms race among NVIDIA, TSMC, and Samsung with limited competition and high switching costs. At a 33.8x forward PE with 13.2% YoY revenue growth, the valuation reflects execution risk on whether ASML can scale production to meet explosive demand from AI infrastructure buildout without supply chain constraints.

stocks.name: Intel
stocks.thesis: Intel's foundry segment is positioned to capture incremental AI chip manufacturing demand as customers diversify away from TSMC, but execution risk is material given the company's historical process node delays and the need to win design wins at advanced nodes (7nm/5nm/3nm) where TSMC maintains a 2-3 year lead. At a 74.5x forward PE with only 7.2% YoY revenue growth, the market is pricing in aggressive foundry margin expansion and significant AI workload capture that remain unproven at scale.

stocks.name: Eaton
stocks.thesis: Eaton's 16.8% YoY revenue growth positions it as a direct beneficiary of AI data center power infrastructure scaling, with its power distribution and thermal management solutions critical to supporting hyperscaler capex cycles. However, the 25.5x forward PE embeds significant upside already priced in, requiring sustained growth acceleration to justify current valuation multiples relative to historical power equipment comps.

stocks.name: Microsoft
stocks.thesis: Microsoft's 18.3% YoY revenue growth reflects strong execution across Azure AI services and enterprise cloud adoption, positioning it as a primary beneficiary of the multi-year AI infrastructure capex cycle with embedded moat through OpenAI partnership and enterprise stickiness. However, the 23.3x forward PE embeds significant AI upside and leaves limited margin of safety if AI monetization timelines extend or competitive pressures from AWS/GCP intensify.
